Counts came from featureCounts — check whether gene identifiers are Ensembl IDs, Entrez IDs or symbols and record which, since pathway step T2S1 depends on it
steps.question: Do the 6 samples in counts/counts.csv align cleanly with the 6 rows of metadata/metadata.csv, are the values valid integer counts, and do treated vs control separate in PCA without an unmodelled outlier?
constraints: Use R with DESeq2 (installed 1.52.0); do not attempt to install anything
Keep any single script under 300 lines
steps.description: Read counts.csv (12,000 rows x 7 columns — expect one gene-ID column plus 6 sample columns; if the first column is unnamed or an index, treat it as the gene identifier) and metadata.csv (6 rows x 2 columns: sample identifier and condition with levels treated/control). Verify sample names match one-to-one between the two files before any modeling; stop and report if they do not. Cast counts to integer mode, drop all-zero and very low-count genes using a standard independent-filtering threshold (e.g. keep genes with counts >= 10 in at least 3 samples, the size of the smaller group), compute DESeq2 size factors to summarize library-size differences, run variance-stabilizing transformation and produce: (a) per-sample library size and gene-detection table, (b) PCA plot colored by condition, (c) sample-to-sample distance heatmap. This is QC that feeds the DE step; it does not produce the DE results.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 metadata samples matched to exactly one counts column, with mismatches reported explicitly
Filtered count matrix saved as CSV plus VST-transformed matrix for downstream use
PCA plot colored by condition and a sample-distance heatmap saved as PNG
A short QC summary stating library-size range, number of genes before/after filtering, and whether any sample is an outlier in PCA

steps.name: Differential expression treated vs control (DESeq2)
caveats: If any sample shows extreme Cook's-distance outliers, flag them in the summary rather than silently removing them (with 3 vs 3, removal destroys the contrast — report, do not drop)
12,000 genes is small for a STAR/featureCounts run (typical output is ~25-40k): note the count in the summary but do not filter beyond low-count removal
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples (3 vs 3, unpaired, single batch), at BH-adjusted p < 0.05?
constraints: No covariates in the design formula beyond condition
Report the actual number of significant genes; do not relax thresholds to produce a result
steps.description: Build a DESeqDataSet from the filtered count matrix (T1S1) with design ~ condition, using the treated/control factor from metadata.csv. Run DESeq() with the Wald test, apply independent hypothesis filtering via results(), and shrink log2 fold changes with lfcShrink(type='apeglm') for ranking and reporting. Call significant genes at padj < 0.05 with a |log2FC| >= 1 reporting tier (do not treat the fold-change tier as part of the significance call). Produce: full results table (gene ID, baseMean, log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) sorted by padj; volcano plot; MA plot; normalized-count heatmap of the top significant genes; and explicit up/down counts. The design has no covariates: metadata is 2 columns (sample, condition), single batch, unpaired — there is nothing else to adjust for, and none should be invented.
acceptance_criteria: results() contrast is exactly treated vs control with treated as the numerator, stated in the output
Full DE table saved as CSV including all 4 significance tiers (up/down x significant/not) counts in the summary
Volcano and MA plots saved as PNG with padj<0.05 genes highlighted
Shrunk and unshrunk log2FC both retained in the results table
Summary states honestly that with n=3 per group power is limited and only large effects are detectable; report the number of genes at padj<0.05 and at padj<0.1 as a sensitivity tier

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE results (WikiPathways human)
caveats: With ~12,000 genes and low DE counts expected at n=3/group, pathway results may be sparse — interpret as hypothesis-generating
WikiPathways symbol matching is case-sensitive and uses current HGNC symbols; report genes lost to symbol versioning
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among the genes differentially expressed between treated and control, and does the direction of the enriched pathway (normalized enrichment score) agree with the DE direction?
constraints: fgsea with nperm fixed via default multilevel procedure; set a seed for reproducibility
No network access — all inputs are local files
steps.description: Run pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) on the full treated-vs-control gene list ranked by signed statistic (use the apeglm-shrunk log2FC / lfcSE, or stat, from T1S2 — state which). Gene sets: the provisioned human WikiPathways GMT (HGNC gene symbols, species Homo sapiens) — the step must first confirm the reference file exists and matches the organism of the data before relying on it; if the human GMT is absent from the environment, report that pathway interpretation could not be run and end the step gracefully rather than failing. Identifier handling: if the count-matrix gene IDs are not HGNC symbols (featureCounts commonly emits Ensembl gene IDs), map them to symbols with org.Hs.eg.db/AnnotationDbi via clusterProfiler::bitr and report the mapping rate; unmappable genes are dropped from ranking (their statistic values remain in the DE table). Report: per-pathway NES, padj (BH), size, and leading-edge genes for significant pathways; a bar/dot plot of top pathways; and the overlap of leading-edge genes with the top DE genes. Per-gene over-representation analysis (ORA) on the padj<0.05 gene list is run as a secondary check (clusterProfiler enricher against the same GMT) and results compared with fgsea qualitatively.
acceptance_criteria: Reference GMT confirmed present and human before use; if absent, the step reports the gap and exits cleanly (annotation lost, not the run)
Gene-ID-to-symbol mapping rate reported if mapping was needed
fgsea results table (pathway, NES, size, padj, leadingEdge) saved as CSV, ranked by padj
Top-pathway plot saved as PNG
Direction consistency between NES sign and DE direction noted in the summary; if no pathway passes padj<0.25, say so plainly rather than listing nominal hits as findings

plan.title: Liver treated-vs-control DE (STAR/featureCounts) + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is raw integer gene-level counts from STAR + featureCounts (12,000 genes x 6 samples) with a 6 x 2 sample table describing 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired and single-batch. Because the counts come from an aligner + summarizer rather than a transcript quantifier, gene-level count-based differential expression is the correct and only appropriate model — no transcript-level (tximport) step applies. The plan is: (1) import and QC the count matrix against the metadata (sample alignment, library sizes, low-count filtering, PCA on variance-stabilized values to confirm the treated/control contrast dominates unmodelled structure); (2) run DESeq2 negative-binomial differential expression for treated vs control with Wald test, BH FDR correction, and apeglm log2FC shrinkage, reporting up/down gene counts honestly given only n=3 per group (low power, wide CIs); (3) map gene identifiers to HGNC symbols if needed and run pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea) against the provisioned human WikiPathways gene sets to interpret the DE result at pathway level. Steps 1-2 use the installed R DESeq2 stack (DESeq2 1.52.0, apeglm, EnhancedVolcano, ggplot2); step 3 uses fgsea 1.38.0 plus clusterProfiler/org.Hs.eg.db for ID mapping, and degrades to a reported annotation gap rather than failing the run if the GMT is unavailable.
